# federation-resolution

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from libs/openid-federation/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/federation-resolution.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `federation-resolution` component of `libs/openid-federation`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.federation`: generated from its catalogue, [federation-resolution.json](../../libs/openid-federation/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/federation-resolution.json), by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Families: `OIDF_FEDERATION_RESOLUTION_`. A name under one of these that no catalogue declares is an unknown key.

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `FEDERATION`, `AUTO_REGISTRATION` ([components](../development/settings-catalogue.md#components)).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_RESOLUTION_WALL_CLOCK_SECONDS` | `45`; seconds, 1 to 300 | How long one trust chain resolution may spend on the network, from when it starts: every fetch it causes, its peer chain and a Trust Mark validation's issuers and status calls included, ends by then; a resolution that runs out is refused as invalid_trust_chain | **First request**: Not a whole number of seconds from 1 to 300: refused, naming the setting, when a trust chain validator is built - at start-up for most, on the first request that needs one for the rest | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_RESOLUTION_MAX_REQUESTS` | `24`; a whole number, 1 to 256 | How many requests one trust chain resolution may spend: each statement asked for (from the cache or not) and each further request made to answer it, such as an authority's Entity Configuration to find its fetch endpoint | **First request**: Not a whole number from 1 to 256: refused, naming the setting, when a trust chain validator is built - at start-up for most, on the first request that needs one for the rest | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_RESOLUTION_MAX_AUTHORITY_HINTS` | `10`; a whole number, 1 to 64 | How many authority_hints of one Entity Configuration a resolution follows, after the configured trust anchors are moved to the front | **First request**: Not a whole number from 1 to 64: refused, naming the setting, when a trust chain validator is built - at start-up for most, on the first request that needs one for the rest | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_RESOLUTION_MAX_ROUTE_ATTEMPTS` | `8`; a whole number, 1 to 64 | How many routes that reach a trust anchor a resolution validates in full before it reports the first one's failure | **First request**: Not a whole number from 1 to 64: refused, naming the setting, when a trust chain validator is built - at start-up for most, on the first request that needs one for the rest | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_RESOLUTION_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS` | `60`; seconds, 0 to 300 | The leeway allowed on an Entity Statement's iat and exp when a chain is validated | **First request**: Not a whole number of seconds from 0 to 300: refused, naming the setting, when a trust chain validator is built - at start-up for most, on the first request that needs one for the rest | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_RESOLUTION_RESOLVE_SUBJECTS_PER_MINUTE` | `30`; a whole number, 1 to 10000 | How many distinct subjects the resolve endpoint (/federation/resolve) answers for one caller address in any minute: asking about one more is answered 503 temporarily_unavailable with a Retry-After, and asking again about a subject already counted in that minute is not counted again | **First request**: Not a whole number from 1 to 10000: refused, naming the setting, on the first request to the resolve endpoint, which is answered 500 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_RESOLUTION_RESOLVE_CACHE_SECONDS` | `60`; seconds, 0 to 60 | How long the resolve endpoint keeps a resolve response and answers the same request - subject, trust anchors, entity types and authenticated client alike - with it: this many seconds or until the response's exp, whichever is sooner; 0 keeps none | **First request**: Not a whole number of seconds from 0 to 60: refused, naming the setting, on the first request to the resolve endpoint, which is answered 500 | Any | Yes |
